reason: E1 supports that high-density boundaries block dislocations and that tight BCC1/BCC2 binding inhibits interfacial cracks, but it does not provide evidence for an optimal phase ratio, quantified wear rate reduction, or the specific hardness threshold claimed.
premises: Dual-phase BCC microstructure provides high-density grain and phase boundaries that block dislocation motion, enhancing hardness.
Tight binding between BCC1 and BCC2 phases inhibits interfacial crack formation, improving toughness.
The synergistic coupling of hardening and toughening from the two BCC phases reduces material removal during wear.
An optimized dual-phase ratio yields ultrahigh microhardness (>1070 HV) and significantly lower wear rates compared to single-phase coatings.
This mechanism holds when phase boundaries are coherent and well-distributed; excessive imbalance negates benefits.
